exposure: neighborhood-level racial and economic segregation (Index of the Concentration of the Extremes, ICE tertiles)
cohort: The study included 385,825 nulliparous individuals with term, singleton, vertex births of Black, White, and Biracial (Black/White) infants in California between 2011 and 2019.
finding: The low-risk cesarean delivery disparity by race persisted across all levels of neighborhood racial and economic segregation, with both Black and Biracial individuals having a higher risk than White individuals.
mod_finding: The risk of low-risk cesarean delivery was greatest in Black individuals (30.71%), followed by Biracial (25.47%) and White (24.98%), and these racial disparities were consistent across all tertiles of racial and economic segregation.
